items.name: The three ramified quadratic characters at 2
items.statement: On ℤ₂×/(ℤ₂×)² with basis −1,5, the nonzero F₂ characters have values (1,0),(0,1),(1,1) and conductor exponents 2,3,3. For each t∈c, composing with 1↦t gives one allowed map of each kind; add the trivial map.
items.locator: Wood §7 omitted local-2 calculation; derived unit-square-class adapter
items.note: API: enumerate all allowed rank≤1 linear maps, conductor exponent, −1 image, and invariance under a change of square-class basis. Exhaustive finite tests k=1,…,5 compare the enumeration with all homomorphisms from F₂².

items.name: Outside-coset character sum
items.statement: For A=F₂^(k+1), H=kerπ, m=2^k and χ∈A*, ∑_(t∈A\H)χ(t) is m for χ=1, −m for χ=π, and 0 otherwise.
items.locator: Wood §7 character cancellation; explicit finite calculation
items.note: This is finite character orthogonality on H and its nontrivial coset. It simultaneously controls the odd-prime and prime-2 factors. Keep π as the ±1 character (−1)^π when switching additive/multiplicative notation.

items.name: The principal Euler product T
items.statement: For m=2^k, define T(s)=(1+m·2^(−2s)+2m·2^(−3s))∏_(p odd)(1+m p^(−s)) on Re s>1.
items.locator: Wood §7; explicit completion of the exceptional Euler factor
items.note: API: convergence, nonnegative coefficients, finite-prime truncation and equality to the trivial-character contribution. Use existing LSeries/EulerProduct carriers, not a new generic Dirichlet-series definition.

items.name: The quotient-character Euler product U
items.locator: Wood §7; explicit prime-2 and sign calculation
items.note: API: signed coefficient function, absolute convergence, quotient-character contribution and later cancellation. Individual U coefficients need not be nonnegative and do not receive the counting Tauberian theorem directly.

items.name: The remaining-character Euler product V
items.statement: Define V(s)=(1+m·2^(−3s))∏_(p≡1 mod4)(1+m p^(−s)) on Re s>1.
items.note: All 2m−2 characters distinct from 1 and π have this contribution. API: same coefficient/truncation interface as T,U and the exact multiplicity; this vanishes from the imaginary fixed-σ sum because those character values at σ sum to zero.

items.name: Real infinity projector identity
items.statement: The allowed-homomorphism series with infinity image 0 is F+(s)=(T(s)+U(s)+(2m−2)V(s))/(2m).
items.locator: Wood §7 real projector; /110 and local calculations
items.note: Expand 1_(x=0)=|A|⁻¹∑χχ(x). Nonnegative integer coefficients follow from the counting interpretation, not the signed Euler-product presentation. Finite prime sets are checked exactly before the convergent infinite product.

items.name: Imaginary rigid infinity projector identity
items.statement: For distinguished swap σ, the allowed-homomorphism series with infinity image σ is F−(s)=(T(s)−U(s))/(2m). The outside-only series equals mF−.
items.locator: Wood §7 imaginary step, derived via Proposition 4.4 conventions
items.note: Expand 1_(x=σ)=|A|⁻¹∑χχ(σ)χ(x). Here χ=1,π contribute +1,−1 and the other coefficients sum to zero. Linear automorphisms fixing π act transitively on the outside coset, explaining the factor m. This is the required regression against the inherited unnormalized selector.

items.name: Principal product continuation
items.statement: T(s)=ζ(s)^m G_T(s), where G_T is holomorphic on Re s>1/2 and G_T(1)>0.
items.locator: Wood §7 analytic step; explicit Euler-product proof
items.note: At odd p the factor of G_T is (1+m p^(−s))(1−p^(−s))^m=1+O_m(p^(−2Re s)). At 2 use (1+m·2^(−2s)+2m·2^(−3s))(1−2^(−s))^m. Compact-uniform absolute convergence away from a finite prime set proves holomorphy; finite factors are retained as polynomials, without assuming they are zero-free.

items.name: Quotient-character product continuation
items.statement: U(s)=L(s,χ4)^m G_U(s), where G_U is holomorphic on Re s>1/2, so U is holomorphic near every point of Re s=1.
items.note: At odd p the factor is (1+mχ4(p)p^(−s))(1−χ4(p)p^(−s))^m; its linear term cancels. At 2 retain 1−m·2^(−2s). This factor can vanish at s=1 for m=4, so positivity of U or division by its local factor must not be assumed.

items.name: Remaining-character product continuation
items.statement: For k≥1, V(s)=ζ(s)^(m/2)L(s,χ4)^(m/2)G_V(s), where G_V is holomorphic on Re s>1/2; V has pole order at most m/2 at 1 and no other poles on Re s=1.
items.note: At p≡1 mod4 use (1+mz)(1−z)^m, at p≡3 mod4 use (1−z²)^(m/2), and at 2 use (1+m·2^(−3s))(1−2^(−s))^(m/2). Positive integer exponents require k≥1; the k=0 boundary is handled separately.

items.name: Positive common leading coefficient
items.statement: G_T(1)=(1+m/2)2^(−m)∏_(p odd)(1+m/p)(1−1/p)^m>0. Both F+ and F− have an order-m pole at 1 with leading coefficient G_T(1)/(2m).
items.note: Every displayed factor at 1 is positive and the infinite product converges absolutely after linear cancellation. U is holomorphic and V has strictly lower pole order m/2. This proves the positivity rather than treating an unspecified residue as nonzero.

items.name: Integer-pole nondecreasing Laplace Tauberian theorem
items.statement: Let α:[0,∞)→[0,∞) be nondecreasing and locally integrable, with f(s)=∫₀∞e^(−st)α(t)dt convergent for Re s>a>0. Suppose f extends holomorphically near every point on Re s=a except a, where it has an order-m pole with leading coefficient B>0, m≥1. Then α(t)∼B e^(at)t^(m−1)/(m−1)!.
items.locator: Delange (1954), §5.2.1 Theorem III, pp.235–238; standing hypotheses p.213
items.note: Integer specialization of Delange's ω theorem. The local decomposition includes an analytic numerator and holomorphic remainder, not only a radial limit. The proof and its reduction using finite differences were read; no claim that the rest of the 1954 paper was fully extracted.

items.name: Dirichlet summatory function as a Laplace transform
items.statement: For a_n≥0 and F(s)=∑_(n≥1)a_n n^(−s) absolutely convergent for Re s>1, set α(t)=∑_(n≤e^t)a_n. Then ∫₀∞e^(−st)α(t)dt=F(s)/s on Re s>1; at a positive pole s=a the leading coefficient is divided by a.
items.locator: Delange application to Wood §7; direct Tonelli/absolute-convergence adapter
items.note: Use inclusive cutoff and note endpoint values at t=log n do not affect the integral. The n=1 mass is included. For complex s justify the interchange by absolute convergence; replacing F(s)/s by F(s) would lose the positive-abscissa scaling factor.

items.name: Elementary-two series satisfy the full Tauberian hypotheses
items.statement: For k≥1, both F± have nonnegative counting coefficients, converge absolutely on Re s>1, and continue meromorphically to Re s>1/2; on Re s=1 the only pole is at 1, of order m and leading coefficient G_T(1)/(2m).
items.locator: Wood §7, completed analytic input to Delange
items.note: Use the three factorization lemmas, holomorphy of L(s,χ4), and ζ's sole pole at 1. No zero-free theorem is needed because ζ,L appear only to nonnegative integer powers and the residual local factors are polynomials.

items.name: Real elementary-two leading constant
items.statement: The cumulative real rigid-pair numerator for rank k≥1 is asymptotic to C_k X(log X)^(m−1), where m=2^k and C_k=G_T(1)/(2m(m−1)!)>0.
items.locator: Wood §7, explicit constant and surjectivity subtraction
items.note: First apply the generic Delange corollary to all allowed homomorphisms, then remove lower-rank images using the following two items. Equality of the two leading constants is for these rigid conventions; it is not a claim of equal unrigid finite averages.

items.name: Imaginary elementary-two leading constant
items.statement: The cumulative imaginary fixed-swap rigid numerator for rank k≥1 is asymptotic to C_k X(log X)^(m−1), where m=2^k and C_k=G_T(1)/(2m(m−1)!)>0.
items.locator: Wood §7, explicit constant and surjectivity subtraction
items.note: First apply the generic Delange corollary to all allowed homomorphisms, then remove lower-rank images using the following two items. Equality of the two leading constants is for these rigid conventions; it is not a claim of equal unrigid finite averages.

items.name: Rank-zero boundary for surjectivity subtraction
items.statement: For A=C2, allowed homomorphisms with prescribed infinity sign consist of the corresponding quadratic characters and possibly the trivial character. Their cumulative discriminant count is O(X).
items.locator: Wood §7 k=1 boundary; quadratic-field counting input
items.note: This avoids applying the V factorization with m/2=1/2. The usual positive/negative fundamental-discriminant asymptotics give the O(X) bound; the exact leading constants are not needed for this boundary estimate.

items.name: Proper-image contribution is negligible for either projector
items.statement: For k≥1 and any proper image W≤F₂^(k+1) meeting the outside coset, dim W=j+1≤k. Its allowed maps have growth O_k(X(log X)^(2^j−1)); sum over the finitely many W. For the imaginary projector retain only W containing σ. Images inside kerπ give only the trivial map.
items.note: All allowed inertia has outside image, and the abelian Galois group over ℚ is generated by inertia with the global sign relation. Thus a nontrivial allowed image cannot lie inside kerπ. Since 2^j<2^k, the finite sum is little-o of the main term. Use the O(X) rank-zero case when j=0.

items.name: All A4 automorphisms preserve the order-96 type
items.statement: Aut(A4)≅S4 has cardinality 24. Its induced map on A4^ab=C3 is either +1 or −1, so simultaneous application on both factors preserves ker(A4²→C3, (a,b)↦ā+b̄), and commutes with factor swap.
items.locator: Wood Appendix A.1 rigidification; finite-group derivation
items.note: Conjugation by S4 gives 24 distinct automorphisms. A generator of order 3 has eight possible images and a nontrivial V4 element has three; these generators generate A4, so there are at most 24. The scratch test checks both generation and distinct conjugations; no GAP table lookup is needed.

items.name: Eligible class-group kernels and A4 extensions are bijective
items.statement: Fix one S3 normal closure M with quadratic subfield K. Each C3-stable but not S3-stable kernel N of a quotient Cl(M)↠V4 determines one A4 extension L/K not normal over ℚ, and conversely. The unique normal V4 in A4 makes M the unique cyclic cubic intermediate extension, so different eligible M or kernels do not duplicate L.
items.locator: Wood Appendix A.1; class-field equivariance and A4 subgroup structure
items.note: Use the unramified class-field correspondence and /125. Work with embedded subfields in a fixed closure: two distinct normal extensions of K are not K-isomorphic inside that closure. Input cubic fields are isomorphism classes, each giving the S3 closure once.

items.name: Equivalent rigidification weights for the A4 computation
items.statement: For this embedded type, #rigid surjections=24·#eligible kernels=4·#eligible quotient epimorphisms=48·#S3-orbits of eligible kernels.
items.locator: Wood Appendix A.1; derived exact normalization
items.note: Each kernel has |GL₂(F₂)|=6 epimorphisms. A non-S3-stable C3-stable kernel has orbit size two, and all 24 target automorphisms preserve the type. This is a normalization theorem for a correctly specified algorithm, not validation of the paper's implementation.

items.name: Finite S3-module regression for quotient weighting
items.statement: On V=F4², let C3 act by scalar multiplication by a primitive cube root and the involution act coordinatewise by Frobenius x↦x². The C3-stable F₂-codimension-two subspaces are the five F4 lines; precisely three are involution-stable and the other two form one orbit. There are twelve quotient epimorphisms with those two kernels.
items.locator: Derived test for the Appendix A.1 algorithm
items.note: Thus 24·2=4·12=48·1. Enumerate all 4^4 F₂-linear maps to F₂² and their kernels to test independently. This is a synthetic finite module, not asserted to be a particular number-field class group.

items.name: Odd-index-two homology reduction
items.statement: If H⊲F has odd order and F/H=C2, then H₂(F,ℤ)≅H₂(H,ℤ)_(C2). In particular H₂(F,ℤ) has odd order; commuting-pair classes with an involution entry vanish, so H₂(F,c)=H₂(F,ℤ) for a set c of involutions.
items.note: In the Lyndon–Hochschild–Serre homology spectral sequence, H_i(C2,H_j(H,ℤ)) vanishes for i>0,j>0 because the coefficients have odd order; H₂(C2,ℤ)=0 and differentials from 2-primary terms into odd-order H₂(H,ℤ) vanish. The commuting-pair class is killed by the order of either entry. Import the generic spectral-sequence/five-term infrastructure in the parent continuation, not privately in arithmetic statistics.

items.name: Refined conjecture, generator form (corrected Conjecture 5.1)
items.statement: Let Q be ℚ or F_q(t), G finite, G′≤G≀S₂ admissible and good, c the order-two elements of G′ outside ker π, L=Q(μ_{4|G̃′_c|}), and u a generator of μ_L. For every h∈H₂(G′,c)[|μ_Q|], the averages over tame imaginary (resp. real) quadratic K of #{ρ∈Sur(G_K^{un,∞},G) of type G′ with I_{G′,π,Q}(ρ,u)=h} (resp. of pairs (ρ,y) of type G′ with I((ρ,y),u)=h) tend to 1 as the discriminant bound X→∞. Equivalently, by /299, one may stratify by the Hom-valued invariant μ_L→H₂(G′,c)[|μ_Q|], u′↦I(ρ,u′).
items.locator: Conjecture 5.1, p.26, corrected (the printed version allows any u∈μ_L)
items.note: A proposition being conjectured, not a theorem. It is the extraction's correction of /99, recorded in research/blueprint/errata/PAPER-WOOD-19.json (E7). It is not Wood's printed statement. It matches Theorem 4.8, where the function-field component invariants are evaluated at u_q∈Ẑ(1)^×, a generator. API: the conjecture as a Prop with G, G′, Q, u and h explicit; a test that for u=1 the printed variant /99 fails, via /144; a test that the generator choice does not change the family of counts, via /299.

items.name: Generator evaluation identifies the Hom-valued lifting invariant
items.statement: In Definition 3.1, let L=K(μ_{4|F̃_c|}) and let u be a generator of the cyclic group μ_L. Then φ↦I_{F,π,K}(φ,u)∈H₂(F,c)[|μ_K|] and φ↦(u′↦I_{F,π,K}(φ,u′))∈Hom(μ_L,H₂(F,c)[|μ_K|]) determine each other. Evaluation at u is a bijection Hom(μ_L,H₂(F,c)[|μ_K|])→H₂(F,c)[|μ_K|]. For another generator u^λ, λ prime to |μ_L|, I(φ,u^λ)=I(φ,u)^λ, so the stratifications by I(·,u) and I(·,u^λ) differ by the bijection h↦h^λ of H₂(F,c)[|μ_K|].
items.locator: Lemma 3.11 and the discussion after Definition 3.1, pp.12–13; consequence used by /298
items.note: Supplies the justification for the generator form /298 asked for by the previous handoff (item 1). Elementary from Lemma 3.11; no further source needed.

items.name: Square-class obstruction of a component fiber
items.statement: Let F=G′, c a generating union of involution classes c_i, A=H₂(F,c), and F̃_c→F a chosen reduced Schur cover with class-compatible lifts ĝ_i. Fix g∈c∪{1}, lift ĝ (ĝ=1 for g=1), and a nonnegative multidegree n with Σ n_i[c_i]=[g] in F_ab. Set b(g,n)=ĝ²∏_i(ĝ_i²)^{−n_i}∈A and β(g,n)=b(g,n) mod A². All factors are central. This class is independent of lift choices and depends only on the parity vector of n. Abelianization compatibility is imposed separately; an incompatible fiber is empty before the obstruction is tested.
items.locator: Wood19 §4.1 equation(6) and Remark4.2; explicit derived construction

items.name: All discrete-action fixed fibers
items.statement: Let F=G′, c a generating union of involution classes c_i, A=H₂(F,c), and F̃_c→F a chosen reduced Schur cover with class-compatible lifts ĝ_i. Fix g∈c∪{1}, lift ĝ (ĝ=1 for g=1), and a nonnegative multidegree n with Σ n_i[c_i]=[g] in F_ab. For odd q coprime to |F|, put m=(q−1)/2. The number of q-fixed points in the universal marked-extension fiber over (g,n) is |A[q−1]| if b(g,n)^m∈A^{q−1}, and zero otherwise. If the abelianization condition fails, it is zero. The same is true for q^{-1}-fixed points.

items.name: Square-times-torsion solvability test
items.statement: For a finite abelian group A, b∈A and integer m≥1, b^m∈A^{2m} iff b∈A²·A[m]. Consequently the nonempty-fiber condition in /301 is β(g,n) in the image of A[(q−1)/2] in A/A².
items.locator: Elementary consequence of Wood19 equation(6), made explicit for the parity analysis

items.name: Two-primary obstruction threshold
items.statement: For finite abelian A of 2-primary exponent 2^e (e=0 if its 2-primary part is trivial), define t_A(b)=min{t≥0 : b∈A²·A[2^t]}. This lies in [0,e] and depends only on b mod A². The odd-primary part is a square and contributes no obstruction.
items.locator: Derived finite-group interface for Wood19 Remark4.2

items.name: Two-adic criterion for stable fiber survival
items.statement: Let F=G′, c a generating union of involution classes c_i, A=H₂(F,c), and F̃_c→F a chosen reduced Schur cover with class-compatible lifts ĝ_i. Fix g∈c∪{1}, lift ĝ (ĝ=1 for g=1), and a nonnegative multidegree n with Σ n_i[c_i]=[g] in F_ab. For odd q coprime to |F|, the fiber in /301 is nonempty iff v₂(q−1)≥t_A(b(g,n))+1. In a cyclic 2-primary decomposition, t_A(b) is the largest exponent e_j among factors C_{2^{e_j}} where b has odd coordinate, with empty maximum zero. The parities in Proposition4.1 have β=1, hence threshold zero and survive for every allowed q.

items.name: Exact count of stable parity multidegrees
items.statement: Let N≥1, N0≥0, d≥0 and ε∈{0,1}^N. Let a_i be the least integer ≥N0 of parity ε_i. The number of n with n_i≥N0, n_i≡ε_i mod2 and Σn_i=d is binomial(L+N−1,N−1) if L=(d−Σa_i)/2 is a nonnegative integer, and zero otherwise.
items.locator: Wood19 Theorem4.8 parity-vector argument; exact stars-and-bars form

items.name: Whole fixed-degree component profile
items.statement: Fix a centerless admissible F=G′, signature ± and n≥2. Put d=2n−1 and g=swap in the imaginary case, d=2n and g=1 in the real case. For q coprime to |F|, let C_n^±(q) be the total number of Frobenius-fixed geometric components in the disjoint union of CHur^{c,g}_{F,m} over all nonnegative m with Σm_i=d. Set M(q)=|H₂(F,c)[q−1]| and P_n^±(q)=C_n^±(q)/M(q)∈Q≥0. This includes every multidegree, not only the stable orthant.

items.name: Moment differs from whole component profile by a vanishing error
items.statement: In /306, let B_n uniformly bound the total number of geometric components and K_d be the component error constant of Theorem4.7. Then |Ẽ_n^±(q)/M(q)−P_n^±(q)|≤B_n(K_d q^{−1/2}+q^{−1})/(1−q^{−1}). In particular the difference is O_n(q^{−1/2}). One can take B_n=D_d from the finite-étale degree bound /314.
items.locator: Derived by summing Wood19 Theorem4.7 over all components and using exact §4.8 denominators

items.name: Ordinary-limit existence is eventual profile constancy
items.statement: Under /306–/307, the ordinary limit of Ẽ_n^±(q)/M(q), as allowed prime powers q→∞, exists iff P_n^±(q) is eventually equal to one rational value. If so that value is the limit. This is a criterion, not a proof that every bad type satisfies it.
items.locator: Derived finite-profile criterion for the gap in Wood19 Theorems1.2/4.8

items.name: Liminf and limsup from recurrent profile values
items.statement: Under /306–/307, let R_n^± consist of rational profile values attained for arbitrarily large allowed q. This is a nonempty finite set. The liminf of Ẽ_n^±(q)/M(q) is min R_n^± and its limsup is max R_n^±. Therefore the existing bad-type bound /97 is a lower bound for every recurrent profile value, not proof that there is only one.
items.locator: Derived strengthening of the explicit liminf interface in Wood19 §4.4

items.name: Boundary component remainder
items.statement: In /306 fix the stable threshold N0 of Theorem4.5(3). Split C_n(q)=C_stable,n(q)+C_boundary,n(q), where stable means every m_i≥N0 and boundary means at least one m_i<N0. Define the normalized remainder R_boundary,n(q)=C_boundary,n(q)/M(q)≥0. No cyclotomic-only formula for this remainder is assumed.
items.locator: Wood19 Theorem4.8 discarded strata, made explicit

items.name: Finite subsets of T1 spaces are discrete
items.statement: For a T1 topological space X and finite s⊂X, the subtype s has discrete topology. Apply this to the finite rational profile image in R; do not build a second generic convergence theory.

items.name: Convergence to a pure filter is eventual equality
items.statement: For a function f:α→β, a filter l on α and b∈β, Tendsto f l (pure b) iff ∀ᶠx in l, f x=b. After /311, this is the discrete-limit interface used for the finite profile.
items.locator: Mathlib/Order/Filter/Tendsto.lean:240–242, statement and proof read at pinned commit

items.name: Complete stable-range component sum
items.statement: Let F=G′, c a generating union of involution classes c_i, A=H₂(F,c), and F̃_c→F a chosen reduced Schur cover with class-compatible lifts ĝ_i. Fix g∈c∪{1}, lift ĝ (ĝ=1 for g=1), and a nonnegative multidegree n with Σ n_i[c_i]=[g] in F_ab. Assume F is centerless and take the stable threshold N0 of Theorem4.5(3). At total degree d, sum the exact composition count /305 over parity vectors ε compatible with [g] in F_ab and satisfying v₂(q−1)≥t_A(b(g,ε))+1. The sum is exactly C_stable,d^g(q)/|A[q−1]|. It does not include C_boundary.
items.locator: Wood19 Theorem4.5(3), Proposition4.1/Remark4.2 and Theorem4.8; derived full stable-range algorithm

items.name: Uniform component bound from the finite-étale Hurwitz degree
items.statement: For fixed centerless F and total branch degree d, let D_d be the rank of the finite-étale map CHur_{F,d}→Conf_d over Z[1/|F|] in Theorem4.5(1). The rank is constant because Conf_d over that base is connected. Over every algebraically closed residue field of allowed characteristic, CHur_{F,d} has at most D_d connected components. The disjoint union of the fixed-infinity, fixed-c multidegree subschemes with total degree d therefore has at most D_d geometric components, independently of q.
items.locator: Wood19 Theorem4.5(1) and (2); EVW12 §8.6.2; explicit degree bound derived here
items.note: This avoids requiring an extra H^0 comparison just to bound the number of components. The per-component error estimate still uses the source's cohomological comparison.

items.name: Product-one component monoid adapter
items.statement: For a finite group F, let Comp(F) be the graded monoid of braid orbits of product-one tuples in F, including the empty tuple. Multiplication is concatenation; it is commutative for product-one tuples. Via marked Hurwitz schemes over Q unramified at infinity, it carries a continuous Galois action preserving degree and the exact monodromy subgroup. This is the product-one submonoid of the general braid monoid /255, not a second braid theory.
items.locator: Seguin, Fields of Definition of Components of Hurwitz Spaces, §§2.2.3–2.3.3
items.note: This source uses an unramified marked point at infinity, unlike Wood's imaginary ramified-infinity locus.

items.name: Galois equivariance for nested-monodromy gluing
items.statement: Let K be a number field and x,y∈Comp(F) have monodromy subgroups Hx,Hy with Hx⊆Hy. Then for every σ∈Gal(Qbar/K), σ(xy)=(σx)(σy). In particular if x,y are defined over K, so is xy.
items.note: Seguin's complete proof was read; the original Cau2012 Theorem3.2 proof remains an explicit prerequisite, not a closed source dependency.

items.name: Bounded-core Galois reduction for product-one components
items.statement: Let F be finite, ψ(F)=Σ_(g∈F)ord(g), K a number field and x∈Comp(F) of monodromy H. There are g1,…,gr∈H and y∈Comp(F), with monodromy H and deg(y)≤ψ(F), such that x=∏i(gi repeated ord(gi) times)·y. For every σ∈Gal(Qbar/K), σx=∏i(gi^{χ(σ^{-1})} repeated ord(gi) times)·σy.
items.locator: Seguin Proposition6.1 and its full preceding proof
items.note: Characteristic-zero result; no comparison with all finite-field Frobenius actions is asserted.

items.name: Finite Galois quotient controlling product-one components
items.statement: For fixed finite F, take the joint finite action of Gal(Qbar/Q) on all components of degrees ≤ψ(F), together with its cyclotomic character modulo exp(F). The kernel of this action acts trivially on every component in Comp(F). Thus the action on all product-one components factors through one finite quotient, independent of degree.
items.note: Turning this quotient into a finite-field Frobenius computation requires the integral moduli/specialization comparison and actual small-component Galois action. No claim that the action depends only on q modulo exp(F).

items.name: Involution-only bounded-core specialization
items.statement: Let c be a union of involution conjugacy classes of a finite F. Every x∈Comp(F) represented by a product-one c-tuple admits the /317 factorization with each gi∈c and y again a product-one c-tuple with the same monodromy and degree ≤ψ(F). Its power blocks (gi,gi) are defined over Q. Consequently the action on all such components factors through the finite permutation action on c-components of degree ≤ψ(F).
items.locator: Derived restriction of Seguin Proposition6.1 and Corollary2.13(iii)
items.note: This addresses a characteristic-zero real/product-one candidate only. Appending Wood's imaginary boundary involution introduces a distinguished branch point, so applying the unrestricted product-one braid quotient would lose data.

items.name: Goursat classification of subdirect products
items.statement: If H≤G₁×G₂ projects onto both factors, N₁={g:(g,1)∈H} and N₂={g:(1,g)∈H} are normal and H is the full inverse image of the graph of an isomorphism G₁/N₁≃G₂/N₂. No finiteness hypothesis is required.
items.locator: Mathlib/GroupTheory/Goursat.lean, pinned 082e2d37e8b0463410cdb532e111cd43d5a66174, full file read 23 September 2026

items.name: Swap-stable quotient graph for an embedded type
items.statement: For a group G, a normal N≤G and α∈Aut(G/N) with α²=id, put H(N,α)={(a,b):α(aN)=bN}. It is a swap-stable subdirect subgroup of G². Define F(N,α)=H(N,α)⋊⟨τ⟩≤G≀C₂ with τ the fixed factor swap. For finite G, |F|=2|G||N|.
items.locator: Derived enumeration adapter for Wood §8, journal pp.417–420; imports pinned Goursat rather than rebuilding it

api.statement: (a,b)∈H iff α(aN)=bN; export the restricted projection surjections and both axis kernels N.

api.name: swap_quotientGraph
api.statement: Factor swap sends H(N,α) to H(N,α⁻¹); supply its action when α²=id.

api.statement: For finite G, card(F(N,α))=2·card(G)·card(N).

api.name: transport_quotientGraph
api.statement: For β∈Aut(G), transport N to β(N) and conjugate α through G/N≃G/β(N); the resulting embedded F is the diagonal β-image.

items.name: Completeness of the swap-stable Goursat enumeration
items.statement: Every subgroup F≤G≀C₂ containing τ and with its base kernel H projecting onto G is F(N,α) for a unique normal N and unique α∈Aut(G/N) with α²=id. Conversely every /321 candidate satisfies these two properties; admissibility additionally requires the generation test /323.
items.locator: Derived from pinned Goursat and Wood admissibility, journal pp.378,386–387

items.name: Exact outside-involution filter for admissibility
items.statement: In F(N,α), the outside involutions are precisely c(N,α)={((a,a⁻¹),τ):α(aN)=a⁻¹N}. For finite G, F(N,α) is admissible iff |⟨c(N,α)⟩|=2|G||N|. Thus enumerating all normal N, all quotient automorphisms with α²=id and this generation test exhausts actual embedded admissible types, before any identification up to isomorphism.
items.locator: Derived complete finite algorithm for Wood Table 1, journal p.418

items.name: Centralizer-generator reduction of the Schur relations
items.statement: Let S→F be a central extension with kernel A and c a conjugacy-invariant subset. The subgroup of A generated by commutators of lifts of all commuting pairs (x,y), x∈c, equals that generated using one x per F-conjugacy class in c and a generating set for C_F(x). In a Schur cover this computes exactly the quotient H₂(F,c).
items.locator: Derived algorithm lemma for Wood §2.3, journal p.387; GAP 4.15.1 EpimorphismSchurCover interface read in lib/schur.gd

items.name: Diagonal automorphism transport of quotient-graph types
items.statement: For β∈Aut(G), let β̄:G/N≃G/β(N). The diagonal action of β on G≀C₂ takes F(N,α) to F(β(N),β̄αβ̄⁻¹), fixes τ and takes its outside-involution set bijectively to that of the transported type. Admissibility, outside-class count and reduced multiplier are preserved.
items.locator: Derived transport API for Wood §8 embedded-type qualification, journal pp.417–420

items.name: Abstract invariance of the good-type involution set
items.statement: For an admissible good type F with its quotient π:F→C₂, the abelianization is C₂ and ker π=[F,F]. Consequently c is precisely the involutions outside [F,F]. Any abstract isomorphism between good admissible types carries their c sets to each other, so H₂(F,c) and |Z(F)| depend only on the abstract group F in this good case. This does not assert the corresponding statement for non-good types.
items.locator: Derived from Wood Lemma 6.2, journal p.414, and the reduced quotient, p.387

items.name: Existing elementary two-quotient carrier
items.statement: For a commutative group A, reuse TauCeti.ElementaryTwoQuotient A=ModN (Additive A)2, its ZMod2-module structure, class map, square criterion and product rule. The quotient A/A² is distinct from the subgroup A[2].

items.statement: Every homomorphism of commutative groups A→B induces a ZMod2-linear map A/A²→B/B²; an isomorphism induces a linear equivalence, with the expected representative formula.

items.statement: For a linear map f:V→W over a division ring, with V finite-dimensional, finrank(range f)+finrank(ker f)=finrank(V).

items.statement: For a finitely generated vector space V over a division ring K, Nat.card V=(Nat.card K)^finrank K V. Here K=F2 and V is finite-dimensional.

items.name: Involution classes span an elementary abelian abelianization
items.statement: If a finite group F is generated by a union c of N conjugacy classes of involutions, F_ab is an elementary abelian2-group and the map a:F2^N→F_ab sending e_i to the class of c_i is surjective.

items.name: Lift squares give well-defined class columns
items.statement: For the chosen reduced Schur cover E→F with kernel A and involution classes c_i, the square of a lift of any x∈c_i lies in A and its image s_i∈A/A² is independent of the lift and of x in the class.

items.name: Binary parity and lift-square linear maps
items.statement: Under /331–332 set V=F2^N, U=F_ab, B=A/A². Define linear maps a:V→U by a(e_i)=[c_i] and s:V→B by s(e_i)=s_i. Only the second map on the free vector space is extended linearly; no nonabelian square homomorphism is used.

items.name: Compatible parities and the obstruction form an affine fiber
items.statement: With /333, for g=1 put v_g=0, and for g∈c_k put v_g=e_k. Compatible epsilon satisfy a(epsilon)=a(v_g), so they form v_g+ker a. Their obstruction /300 is beta(g,epsilon)=s(v_g+epsilon).

items.statement: For a finite abelian A, let B=A/A² and B_t be the image of A[2^t] in B for t≥0. It is an increasing sequence of F2-subspaces, with B_0=0. If the2-primary exponent of A is2^e then B_e=B.

items.name: All surviving parities are a linear-kernel coset
items.statement: For t≥0 define L_t:V→U⊕(B/B_t) by v↦(a(v),s(v) mod B_t). If q is an odd prime power coprime to |F| and v2(q−1)=t+1, the parities whose discrete-action fibers are nonempty are exactly C_t^g=v_g+ker L_t. Each such fiber has |A[q−1]| points.

items.name: Ranks count surviving parities and exact thresholds
items.statement: Under /336, |C_t^g|=2^(N−rank L_t). The real and imaginary signatures have equal surviving-parity cardinalities by translation, but need not have equal weight enumerators or fixed-degree counts. If K_t=2^(N−rank L_t) and K_(-1)=0, the number with exact threshold t is K_t−K_(t−1).

items.statement: For the finite set C_t^g⊂F2^N and an integer N0≥0, define W_t^g(X)=Σ_(epsilon∈C_t^g) X^wt(epsilon+delta·1), with delta=N0 mod2. This polynomial records the least allowed multiplicities of each parity above N0.

items.name: Weight-polynomial formula for the entire stable orthant
items.statement: Assume additionally that F is centerless and N0 is a valid stable threshold in Wood Theorem4.5(3). For fixed allowed q and t=v2(q−1)−1, the formal series of normalized stable component counts is Σ_(d≥0)(C_stable,d^g(q)/|A[q−1]|)X^d = X^(N*N0) W_t^g(X)/(1−X²)^N. This counts only multidegrees with every coordinate at least N0.

items.statement: The exact GAP run covers every embedded admissible candidate from every abstract G of order2 through15 (65 candidates), plus every candidate for G=S4 and the dihedral group of order18 (15 each). For both g=1 and g=tau, every compatible parity has threshold0 in each of these95 candidates. This is computational evidence for a finite target; no universal vanishing theorem is asserted.
